channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: Inside the grind: The SF startup racing to build an AI software engineer
item.description: It’s always war time at Cognition, the startup gunning to beat OpenAI and Anthropic in the coding race.

item.title: Anyone saying SF’s music scene is dead isn’t looking very hard
item.description: It’s devastating that Bottom of the Hill and Thee Parkside are closing. But from North Beach to Hayes Valley to the Mission, small, independently operated venues have shows every night of the week.

item.title: Tony Vitello’s bullpen management can make or break his debut season with the Giants
item.description: Bruce Bochy expressed confidence in the rookie manager and said Buster Posey’s decision to hire a college coach is “not a risk.”

item.title: Check out this Cole Valley compound with “secret garden” vibes
item.description: The three-unit sale includes a duplex and a standalone modern home, complete with a hideaway hot tub.

item.title: Zoox expands into San Francisco’s Marina, North Beach, and Chinatown
item.description: But most San Franciscans still can’t catch a ride — unless they work at Zoox, know someone who does, or make it off the waitlist.

item.title: Giants rookie Daniel Susac throws a family reunion for the ages at Oracle Park
item.description: With his brother Andrew, a former Giants catcher, watching from the stands, the younger Susac recorded the first hits of his MLB career in a win over the Mets.

item.title: SoMa sees homeless surge as tents fall citywide
item.description: People in crisis say they have nowhere to go, but neighbors are tired of being stuck in “containment zones for the city’s problems.”

item.title: I lived through Google’s AI-military crisis. Here’s why engagement still matters
item.description: Deep collaboration between AI companies and the military is harder than withdrawal and harder than compliance. It’s also the best option.

item.title: PST: The end of BART? Inside the Bay Area’s transit crisis
item.description: BART and Muni face historic deficits. Stations could close; lines could vanish. Two November ballot measures may be their only lifeline.

item.title: Tahoe avalanche: investigators cite route, group size in disaster
item.description: But investigators admit that much remains to be known about the deadliest avalanche in California

item.title: Valkyries President Jess Smith is ready to go ‘bigger and bolder’ in Year 2
item.description: More than 90% of season ticket-holders renewed their plans for 2026.

item.title: The Valkyries built a winner through the expansion draft. Now they’re losing talent
item.description: A year after building the core of their roster, Golden State watched Carla Leite and María Conde leave the organization Friday.

item.title: Trump proposed to put Alcatraz in the budget. Year one alone: $152 million.
item.description: Local leaders have rejected the idea of transforming the tourist destination, but the White House says it’s a priority.

item.title: ‘Section 415’ podcast: The 49ers are entering the next phase of their offseason
item.description: Before turning their attention to the NFL Draft, John Lynch and Kyle Shanahan met with reporters to discuss the team’s recent additions.

item.title: Trump czar David Sacks gave Lurie-allied SF group his money. Now he wants it back
item.description: But there’s a snag, says GrowSF: The cash is already spent.
